items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for ring maps A -> B and A -> C the map L_{B x C/A} -> L_{B/A} (+) L_{C/A} is an isomorphism in D(B x C) (source lines 1278-1283). Although the author notes that this follows from the fundamental triangle, the counted proof is the direct elementary one: it factors A -> B x C through A[x] with x mapping to (1, 0), applies the special-case triangle to obtain three distinguished triangles, reduces to the case of B x C over A[x], and then uses flatness of A[x] -> A[x, x^{-1}], the identifications of the localizations of B x C and C, and the flat base change lemma for the cotangent complex to see that the map becomes an isomorphism after inverting x and after inverting x - 1.
